claims.text: Incorporating WS2 particles into a ceramic matrix produces a self-lubricating composite.
The WS2-containing ceramic composite maintains low friction across a wide temperature range.
The WS2-containing ceramic composite exhibits reduced wear across a wide temperature range.
WS2 has an inherently layered structure.
Easy shear between WS2 planes provides low-friction lubrication.
The ceramic matrix preserves the composite's mechanical strength and integrity at elevated temperatures.
The combination of WS2 lubrication and ceramic-matrix integrity balances lubrication efficiency with mechanical strength.
The WS2-containing composite will have a consistently lower friction coefficient than a ceramic matrix without WS2 across a broad temperature range.
The WS2-containing composite will have lower wear rates than a ceramic matrix without WS2 across a broad temperature range.
A ceramic matrix without WS2 is expected to exhibit higher friction and greater wear at elevated temperatures.
Performance under extreme oxidizing atmospheres may differ from performance under the proposed high-temperature sliding conditions.
Interfacial bonding, WS2 particle dispersion, and oxidation can influence the composite's tribological properties.
